title: No Kohli. No Certainty on Rohit. India's Batting Order Walks Into Its First Home Test Without a Safety Net.
excerpt: India's Test against Afghanistan at Mohali begins Saturday without Virat Kohli, with Rohit Sharma's fitness uncertain, and with Rishabh Pant stripped of the vice-captaincy. The batting order that walks out will be the most untested India have fielded at home in years.
body:
When India take the field at the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in Mohali on Saturday for the one-off Test against Afghanistan, the batting order will look unfamiliar. Virat Kohli, who aggravated a hamstring strain while batting through the IPL final, has been ruled out. Rohit Sharma, who chose to train independently in Mohali rather than report to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, is expected to present himself for a fitness clearance only on June 8 — two days into the Test. Rishabh Pant has been stripped of the vice-captaincy.

This is not the India batting lineup that has dominated home Tests for the past decade. It is a lineup in transition, being asked to prove itself against an Afghanistan side that has nothing to lose and everything to gain from its first Test against India in eight years.

The Kohli-Rohit Vacuum

India have not played a home Test without both Kohli and Rohit available since 2014. Even when one has been rested or injured, the other has anchored the batting. Now, for the first time in a generation, India's most experienced batting pair may both be absent from a home Test. Even if Rohit passes his fitness test and plays, his preparation has been unconventional at best — training on his own terms, outside the national setup, at the venue rather than the NCA.

Kohli's absence is confirmed. He played through the hamstring injury in the IPL final — scoring a characteristically defiant 75 not out — but the decision to push through has cost India their most reliable Test batter for the Afghanistan series and the three ODIs that follow. Ruturaj Gaikwad has been called up as his replacement.

Shubman Gill Carries the Weight

With the senior batters unavailable, the onus falls squarely on Shubman Gill. The 26-year-old has the talent to dominate but has not yet proven he can carry a batting lineup when the pressure concentrates entirely on him. In the IPL, he led Gujarat Titans to the final. In Tests, his record is promising but not yet definitive — flashes of brilliance separated by periods of inconsistency.

Gill will likely be joined by a middle order that includes KL Rahul, whose own form has been a subject of debate, and potentially Ishan Kishan, whose recall to the ODI squad after nearly three years signals the BCCI's awareness that the batting cupboard needs restocking. Whether Kishan features in the Test side depends on selection combinations, but the broader message is clear: India are exploring options beyond the old guard.

Pant's Demotion

Rishabh Pant's removal from the vice-captaincy adds a layer of intrigue. His coaches at Lucknow Super Giants have publicly stated that the issue is not leadership but shot selection — the same criticism that has followed Pant throughout his career. In Tests, where patience is rewarded and recklessness punished, Pant's ability to switch gears remains his greatest asset and his most persistent vulnerability.

Without the vice-captaincy tag, Pant is free to focus purely on batting. Whether that freedom helps or hinders him will depend on the match situation. India need him to bat like a senior professional, not a freelancer.

Afghanistan's Opportunity

On the other side, Afghanistan arrive without their talisman Rashid Khan but with genuine ambition. Captain Hashmatullah Shahidi leads a side that has grown significantly since their last Test against India. Their spinners will be keen to test India's middle order on a Mohali pitch that has historically offered assistance to slow bowlers as the match progresses.

For Afghanistan, this is an opportunity to announce themselves as a genuine Test nation. A competitive performance — even without a result — would validate years of investment in their red-ball programme. A win, however unlikely, would be the single greatest result in Afghan cricket history.

What NRI Fans Should Watch

For diaspora fans tuning in from North America and Europe, this Test is a window into Indian cricket's future. The batters who step up in Mohali — or fail to — will shape the team's direction through the World Test Championship and into the 2027 cycle. The era of Kohli-Rohit dominance is ending, whether through injury, age, or the natural passing of generations. What replaces it starts here.

The Test begins Saturday at 9:30 AM IST. Sony Sports Network will carry the broadcast live.
